title: Audit hash-chain writes can fork under concurrent writes and verification does not cover all scopes

original_titles.title: Audit hash chain can fork under concurrent same-scope writes
Audit hash-chain head not serialized per event scope
Concurrent audit writes can fork the hash chain, making audit_verify report a false break
Audit chain verification covers only global scope of the app DB; GT audit rows land in the separate GT database
Audit-chain verification is an admin endpoint, not a CI-enforced tool

problem: audit_write reads the latest hash for event_scope without locking a per-scope chain head. Concurrent transactions can read the same previous hash and append two entries. The verify endpoint invokes audit_verify with the default global scope, while writes use event, challenge, review and scoring scopes.
impact: The append-only hash chain can become inconsistent under ordinary concurrent traffic, and a successful global verification can miss breaks in other scopes.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Add audit.chain_heads with one row per event_scope and a foreign key/last_seq/last_hash. Ensure the head row is created atomically if absent.
Inside the caller’s transaction, lock that scope’s head row FOR UPDATE (or use pg_advisory_xact_lock on a stable scope hash), read last_hash, insert entry and update head in the same transaction.
Make sequence ordering scope-local and document how global, event, challenge, review and GT scopes map to verifiers.
Change the verification endpoint to enumerate all scopes and return per-scope status plus a combined integrity result. Do not silently default to global only.
Add a concurrent writer test with dozens of simultaneous inserts in one scope and a second test verifying all scopes after mixed writes.

acceptance_criteria: Concurrent writes create one linear hash chain per scope.
Verification checks all active scopes and reports first break/scope.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
